subject: tu:game/sound/sounds
value:
PHASE 3 of work_claim.split-map-correction.20260904.v1: the PLAN for the sounds_evt + sounds merge, records only, NO EDITS MADE (neither TU is owned by this lane; measured and written at 1a7f0393e).

THE PREMISE HOLDS, and by a stronger test than the one its own record proposed. claim.BE_the-enemy-gauntworld-blob-aliasing-is-not-aliasing-it-is-a-text-split-misassignment-inside-gamemain.20260904.v1 reports that game/sound/sounds_evt.c and game/sound/sounds.c both materialise base lbl_80114A48 and reads that as ONE object split across two source files. Re-measured with the per-function datum census that settled the gauntworld block (every lbl_ symbol each function references in the dtk split asm, `build/GUNE5D/asm/game/sound/*.s`, window 0x80114800..0x80115400): sounds_evt has exactly ONE function in the window, AudioSetupBossStreams, and it reads lbl_80114A48; sounds has seven, of which AudioBuildMusicName also reads lbl_80114A48 while InitNameAudio, AudioSecretProc, ShopMusicStart, MapMusicStart, AudioRegisterNameBanks and AudioSetupLevelStreams read 0x80114C54..0x80114CE0. Two separately compiled objects each emit their OWN .rodata section, so they cannot both offset from one datum object. One object.

THE FALSIFIER THAT RECORD PUBLISHED DOES NOT DECIDE ANYTHING, and this is worth banking before someone runs it. It reads: 'if the GC .text runs 0x8009C2CC..0x800A00A0 and 0x800A00A0..0x800A18E8 sum to something other than SOUNDS.OBJ's Xbox .text size, the one-object reading is wrong.' Measured: SOUNDS.OBJ's Xbox segment-1 rows are 172 functions summing 0x3A25 (14885 bytes) over a span 0x00076D20..0x0007ACD5 = 0x3FB5 (16309); the two GC runs are 0x3DD4 (15828) + 0x1848 (6216) = 0x561C (22044). The GC figure is 35% larger, which is the ordinary PPC-vs-x86 code-size ratio, not evidence of a second module. A cross-ISA byte-size comparison has no threshold that separates 'same TU' from 'different TU', so the test can only ever be failed. The DECIDABLE falsifier is the datum one: if a function of sounds_evt.c and a function of sounds.c ever stop sharing a materialised base symbol, or a re-dumped PDB produces a second game sound module (`grep '^== .*[Ss][Oo][Uu][Nn][Dd]' research/xbox_symbols/functions_by_module.txt` returns exactly one row today, `.\Release\SOUNDS.OBJ` at line 2999), the reading is wrong.

THE MERGE, as commands and exact numbers.
(1) configure.py: today lines 483-484 are `Object(NonMatching, "game/sound/sounds_evt.c", cflags=cflags_demo)` and `Object(NonMatching, "game/sound/sounds.c", cflags=cflags_demo)`. The merge deletes ONE of them; the survivor must be the one whose .text run comes FIRST in the image, i.e. sounds_evt.c (0x8009C2CC), because the link order in build.ninja follows the Object list and the merged object must land at 0x8009C2CC.
(2) config/GUNE5D/splits.txt: sounds_evt.c currently declares extab 0x80006F18..0x800072B0, extabindex 0x8000AEF4..0x8000B458, .text 0x8009C2CC..0x800A00A0; sounds.c declares extab 0x800072B0..0x800073A0, extabindex 0x8000B458..0x8000B5C0, .text 0x800A00A0..0x800A18E8. The three pairs are ADJACENT in all three sections, so the merge is the trivial one: sounds_evt.c takes extab 0x80006F18..0x800073A0, extabindex 0x8000AEF4..0x8000B5C0, .text 0x8009C2CC..0x800A18E8, and the sounds.c stanza is deleted entirely. No boundary has to be discovered; unlike the gauntworld move, nothing is cut mid-run.
(3) Source: sounds.c's function definitions append to sounds_evt.c IN THAT ORDER (sounds_evt's .text run precedes sounds'), and src/game/sound/sounds.c is deleted. Its declaration preamble ports with it.
(4) Only then do the 25 blob sites (19 in sounds_evt, 6 in sounds) become convertible, because a single object emits a single .rodata prefix from source -- which is exactly the condition attempt.BE_sounds-evt-boss-stream-blob-conversion-rebases-the-pool-and-regresses.20260904.v1 measured the absence of.

RISKS, ranked, and the first two are measured facts from the gauntworld move rather than predictions.
(a) INLINING. Merging makes every sounds.c function visible to every sounds_evt.c caller and vice versa. claim.law.SM_moving-a-function-between-tus-changes-inlining-in-both-directions-and-the-dont-inline-bracket-belongs-on-the-caller.20260904.v1 cost three separate repairs on a 24-function move; a 2-file merge of this size should expect more. The gate is `python tools/gdl/fuzzy.py game/sound/sounds_evt` before and after, row by row -- NOT the DOL checksum, which stays green throughout because both TUs are NonMatching.
(b) WEBFRANK. Each TU carries one pin -- sounds_evt::AudioPlayerEatSFX and sounds::AudioAmbientUpdate. The merge MOVES AudioAmbientUpdate's pin between unit keys in config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json, and webfrank fails CLOSED on a pin whose function is absent from the unit: measured this run at the split-boundary change alone, `KeyError: "symbol 'DoWorldAnimation' not found"` from webfrank.py line 4403. The pin migration is not optional and it is not deferrable to a later commit.
(c) POOL RENUMBER. Appending ~50 functions renumbers sounds_evt's anonymous pool; any permutation pin in either unit needs `python tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_rederive_pin.py <unit> <fn> --apply` plus `python configure.py`. Neither of these two pins is a permutation rule today, so this may cost nothing -- verify, do not assume.
(d) SOURCE ORDER. sounds_evt.c and sounds.c are both NonMatching and their textorder state must be measured before and after (`python tools/gdl/textorder.py game/sound/sounds_evt game/sound/sounds`), because the merge concatenates two orderings into one and can only be judged against the merged target run.
